column1: # Swedish (sv) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); the translation lists the
#                                 language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Combined from the community Swedish catalogs in #5985 and #9536: each row takes the best of their
# translations, with one term per concept across the UI (lager, markering, mask, gradient,
# fjädring, ombilda, rutnät, stödlinje, rityta …); the contested terms follow a native Swedish
# speaker's answers to a terminology questionnaire (#10021). Clean-room: written from the plain
# meaning of the English labels; no proprietary localisation resource was consulted or copied.
# Labels use sentence case, commands are imperatives and the user is addressed as "du". Product,
# format and technology names (PhotoCraft, ArtCraft, OpenType, CMYK, Lab …) and key caps keep their
# spelling; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept. Plural rule: one|other (n != 1 -> other).
# Native-speaker review of the remaining specialist terms is welcome.
# Layer Mask Display Options (the layer mask rubylith's colour and opacity)
# Channel Options and New Spot Channel (#3761)
